questions.question: Which statement about the origin and development of this PIC/S PE 011-1 GDP guide is correct?

options.A: Based on WHO Technical Report Series No. 957, rewritten as a version applicable outside the EU
options.B: Based on the EU GDP guidelines (2013/C 343/01), adapted by a PIC/S expert circle with EU-specific references removed
options.C: Based on ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, expanded into requirements covering the whole distribution process
options.D: Written entirely anew by PIC/S independently, without reference to any existing EU or international guidelines

questions.explanation: The introduction explains that the guide is based on the EU GDP guidelines, adapted by the PIC/S GDP expert circle, with EU-specific references removed. WHO TRS 957 is cited only in Annex 1 for the definition of falsified medicines outside the EU, and ICH Q9 is a reference for quality risk management; neither is the source of this guide.

questions.question: What is the legal effect of PE 011-1 on PIC/S member authorities?

options.A: Once adopted, it automatically becomes law in all PIC/S member countries, which must implement it fully within a deadline
options.B: It is used only for internal training of PIC/S inspectors and is not a guide for industry
options.C: It must be approved case by case by the PIC/S Committee before countries can use it as an inspection basis
options.D: It is a guidance document; whether it becomes a legally binding standard is decided by each member authority

questions.explanation: The guide was adopted by PIC/S as a guidance document, and whether it is converted into a legally binding standard is decided by each Participating Authority. It can also be used for inspection preparation and training, and is not limited to internal use by inspectors.

questions.question: Under the introduction's definition of wholesale distribution, which activity is NOT wholesale distribution?

options.A: Supplying medicinal products directly to the general public (supplying to the public)
options.B: Procuring medicinal products from manufacturers or other wholesalers and holding them in warehouse storage
options.C: Importing medicinal products from another country and supplying them to licensed wholesalers
options.D: Supplying medicinal products to pharmacies or pharmacists authorized to supply the public

questions.explanation: Wholesale distribution includes procuring, holding, supplying, importing, and exporting medicinal products, but expressly excludes supplying medicinal products to the public. Supplying pharmacies, other wholesalers, and the like is wholesale distribution.

questions.question: A manufacturer holds a manufacturing authorization and distributes its own products. According to the introduction, which statement is correct?

options.A: It need not comply with GDP, because the manufacturing authorization exempts it from all distribution-related requirements and checks
options.B: It must comply with GDP only when it outsources delivery to a third-party logistics provider, and not for self-delivery
options.C: It must comply with GDP; the manufacturing authorization covers the authorization to distribute, so no separate wholesale license is needed
options.D: It must comply with GDP and must separately obtain a wholesale distribution authorization in order to distribute its own products

questions.explanation: Holding a manufacturing authorization includes authorization to distribute the products it covers, so a separate wholesale distribution authorization need not be applied for; but whenever a manufacturer carries out any distribution activity for its own products, it must comply with GDP, and is not exempt.

questions.question: Which statement about the scope of this guide is correct?

options.A: It applies to medicinal products for human use and similar products; equivalent attention is recommended for veterinary medicinal products, and it may apply to IMPs
options.B: It applies only to marketed medicinal products for human use; veterinary and investigational medicinal products are expressly excluded and may not be invoked
options.C: It applies compulsorily to both human and veterinary medicinal products, but investigational medicinal products (IMPs) may not be covered by this guide
options.D: It applies only to prescription medicinal products for human use; non-prescription and similar products are outside its scope

questions.explanation: The Scope states that the standards apply to medicinal products for human use and similar products, that equivalent attention to veterinary medicinal products is recommended, and that the guide may also apply to IMPs. For veterinary products it is "recommended" rather than mandatory, which is the trap in the option "applies compulsorily to both human and veterinary medicinal products."

questions.question: Under 1.1 Principle, who is responsible for the distributor's quality system?

options.A: The designated responsible person alone; management need only approve the budget and provide resources
options.B: The quality assurance department has full responsibility, and other departments only cooperate in carrying out its instructions
options.C: The management of the organization, requiring its leadership and active participation, supported by staff commitment
options.D: An external audit body responsible for verification, with management only responding to the deficiencies it raises

questions.explanation: 1.1 states explicitly that the quality system is the responsibility of the organization's management and requires its leadership and active participation, supported by the commitment of staff. The designated person is responsible for implementing and maintaining it but does not replace management's responsibility.

questions.question: Which description of quality risk management (QRM) in this chapter is correct?

options.A: It can be applied both proactively and retrospectively; the effort, formality, and documentation should be commensurate with the risk
options.B: It can be used only after a deviation occurs to investigate root cause; no risk assessment needs to be performed beforehand
options.C: The highest degree of formal procedure and complete documentation is required regardless of the level of risk
options.D: Risk assessment is based mainly on cost and regulatory penalty considerations rather than scientific knowledge and patient protection

questions.explanation: 1.5 explains that QRM is a systematic process for assessing, controlling, communicating, and reviewing quality risks, and can be applied both proactively and retrospectively. Risk assessment must be based on scientific knowledge and process experience and linked to patient protection, and the level of effort should be commensurate with risk, not always the highest.

questions.question: A distributor is small and has simple operations. Under 1.2.5 and 1.2.6, which statement about its change control requirements is most accurate?

options.A: Small organizations may skip establishing change control, with changes implemented after verbal approval by the responsible person
options.B: All changes, large or small, must be revalidated and approved in advance by the regulatory authority
options.C: The degree of change control is decided by the supplier, and the distributor need only passively accept supplier notifications without evaluating them itself
options.D: It must still have a change control system incorporating QRM, with a degree commensurate with the scale and complexity of the activities

questions.explanation: 1.2.6 requires a change control system that incorporates QRM principles and is proportionate and effective; 1.2.5 requires the scale, structure, and complexity of the activities to be considered when establishing or modifying the quality system. A small distributor is therefore not exempt, but adjusts the depth according to risk.

questions.topic: Managing outsourced activities in the quality system
questions.question: A distributor wants to outsource warehousing. Under 1.3, what should the quality system provide for this outsourced activity?

options.A: Only confirm before contract signing that the contract acceptor holds a license, after which performance and quality are managed by the acceptor with no further follow-up
options.B: Assess the contract acceptor's suitability and competence beforehand, define the quality responsibilities and communication processes of both parties, and monitor its performance
options.C: Transfer quality responsibility to the contract acceptor, with the distributor retaining only the right to receive a written report each month
options.D: Review the contract acceptor's operations, and audit if necessary, only when a complaint or deviation occurs

questions.explanation: 1.3 requires the quality system to extend to outsourced activities and to incorporate QRM, including assessing the contract acceptor's suitability and competence, defining responsibilities and communication processes, and monitoring and improving performance periodically. Reviewing only after something goes wrong, or transferring the responsibility away, does not meet the requirement.

questions.question: Under 1.4.1, which of the following should the management's periodic review of the quality system include?

options.A: Only operating performance for the year such as sales volume and inventory turnover, to assess operating effectiveness, as the sole basis for review
options.B: Only deficiencies from external audits and official inspections, with internal performance indicators not included in the review
options.C: It is initiated only after a recall event, and the scope of review is limited to the handling of that recall
options.D: Assessing performance indicators such as complaints, recalls, returns, deviations, CAPA, and outsourced-activity feedback

questions.explanation: The management review in 1.4.1 should, besides measuring achievement of quality objectives, assess performance indicators (complaints, recalls, returns, deviations, CAPA, changes, feedback on outsourced activities, self-assessments, and external assessments) and consider new regulations, innovation, and changes in the business environment. The review is periodic, and its results must be documented in a timely way and communicated internally.

questions.topic: Delegation by the designated responsible person
questions.question: The designated responsible person is traveling and hands the daily approval of returns to a deputy. Under 2.3.2, which statement is correct?

options.A: After delegation, the related responsibility passes to the deputy, the designated person is no longer responsible for the matter, and no record need be kept
options.B: Duties may be delegated, but responsibility may not, and a record of the delegation should be kept
options.C: No duties may be delegated; the designated person must personally perform all approval work
options.D: Delegation is possible only to an outside consultant; internal staff may not stand in for the designated person's duties

questions.explanation: 2.3.2 provides that the designated person may delegate duties but not responsibility; 2.3.5 also requires appropriate records of any delegated duties to be kept. The deputy can therefore do the work, but ultimate responsibility remains with the designated person.

questions.question: Which of the following is a responsibility of the designated responsible person?

options.A: Personally performing every receipt and picking operation, ensuring all stock in and out passes through their hands, including daily handling in the warehouse
options.B: Issuing the company's wholesale distribution authorization and handling its renewal with the regulatory authority
options.C: Deciding product selling prices and customers' commercial terms of trade, and signing sales contracts
options.D: Deciding the final disposition of returned, rejected, recalled, or falsified products, and approving returns back to saleable stock

questions.explanation: The responsibilities listed in 2.3.5 include the final disposition of returned, rejected, recalled, or falsified products and approval of returns to saleable stock, as well as recall coordination, complaint handling, approval of suppliers and customers, and ensuring self-inspections are carried out. Pricing and issuing authorizations are not on the list; issuing authorizations is the competent authority's power.

questions.question: A new warehouse employee will handle temperature-sensitive medicinal products. Under 2.4.4, which statement is correct?

options.A: General GDP training is enough, because temperature control is handled by equipment
options.B: A senior colleague briefs them verbally on site, with no written training procedure needed
options.C: They must receive specific training for products requiring more stringent handling conditions
options.D: Retrain them after the first temperature excursion, for cost-effectiveness

questions.explanation: 2.4.4 requires that personnel handling products requiring more stringent handling conditions receive specific training, for example hazardous substances, radioactive materials, narcotic and psychotropic substances with a risk of abuse, and temperature-sensitive products. 2.4.2 also requires training to follow written procedures and a written training program, and personnel must have adequate competence before starting work.

questions.question: What does 2.2 require regarding organizational structure and responsibility documents?

options.A: An organization chart showing the role and interrelationships of all personnel; key positions must have written job descriptions including deputizing arrangements
options.B: Only the designated responsible person needs a written job description; other personnel are assigned verbally by supervisors, who keep their own records
options.C: The organization chart need only list department names; individual responsibilities are decided by each department, with no separate recording or approval
options.D: Job descriptions take effect only after approval by the regulatory authority, and deputizing arrangements need no records

questions.explanation: 2.2.2 requires an organization chart clearly showing the roles, responsibilities, and interrelationships of all personnel; 2.2.3 requires key positions to have written job descriptions that specify deputising arrangements. 2.1 also stresses that individual responsibilities should be clearly understood by staff and recorded.

questions.question: Under 2.4, besides the GDP requirements themselves, what else should GDP training cover? And how should training records and effectiveness be handled?

options.A: Customer bargaining skills and sales talk; effectiveness is satisfied by the trainee's self-assessment, with no separate evaluation
options.B: Medicinal product pricing regulations and reimbursement rules; effectiveness need only be provided at regulatory inspections
options.C: Product identification and preventing falsified medicines from entering the supply chain; training must be recorded and effectiveness evaluated periodically
options.D: Principles of formulation development; training records are kept by the trainee personally, with no central retention or management

questions.explanation: 2.4.3 requires training to include product identification and the avoidance of falsified medicines entering the supply chain; 2.4.5 requires all training records to be kept and the effectiveness of training to be periodically assessed and documented. An attendance record without an effectiveness assessment is not enough.

questions.question: Under 3.2.4, which group of products MUST always be physically segregated, rather than as determined by risk assessment?

options.A: Falsified, expired, recalled, and rejected products, and products without authorization for the domestic market
options.B: Products pending disposition, returned products, and near-expiry products must all be physically segregated, with no other means permitted
options.C: All complaint products and returned products must be physically segregated regardless of the risk assessment result
options.D: Only falsified and recalled products; expired and rejected products may use an electronic segregation system instead of physical segregation

questions.explanation: 3.2.4 provides that products pending a decision on disposition or removed from saleable stock may be segregated physically or by an equivalent electronic system, with the need for dedicated areas assessed on a risk basis; but at least falsified, expired, recalled, and rejected products and products without domestic market authorization must be physically segregated. In "products pending disposition, returned products, and near-expiry products," the products pending disposition are exactly the category that may be decided by risk assessment.

questions.question: The initial temperature mapping has been completed before a new warehouse is put into use. Under 3.3.2, how should temperature monitoring devices be positioned?

options.A: In the center of the warehouse, the position representing the overall average temperature, to facilitate single-point monitoring
options.B: As recommended in the equipment manufacturer's manual, evenly spaced at each shelf height within the storage area
options.C: According to the mapping results, at the locations showing the greatest temperature fluctuation
options.D: Near the air conditioning outlet, so that temperature changes are detected earliest and responded to in real time

questions.explanation: 3.3.2 requires an initial mapping under representative conditions before the storage area is used, and devices are placed according to the results so that they are located in the areas of extreme fluctuation. After significant changes, mapping is repeated according to a risk assessment.

questions.question: Under 3.4.3, to what should the calibration of equipment used to control or monitor the storage environment be traceable?

options.A: The equipment manufacturer's factory test standard
options.B: A national or international measurement standard
options.C: A reference thermometer designated internally by the distributor
options.D: A calibration laboratory established by the local regulatory authority itself

questions.explanation: 3.4.3 requires calibration to be traceable to a national or international measurement standard; 3.4.2 requires the calibration interval to be determined based on risk and reliability assessment. Alarm settings must be appropriately set, and alarms periodically tested to confirm proper functioning.

questions.question: Under 3.5.4, how should backup data of computerised systems be retained?

options.A: For at least 1 year, stored on the same server for quick restoration and consultation, with no off-site backup needed
options.B: For at least 3 years, stored in a server room in the same building, with no separate site needed
options.C: For at least 10 years, and backup data may be destroyed only with the approval of the regulatory authority
options.D: For the period required by national regulations and at least 5 years, stored at another independent, secure location

questions.explanation: 3.5.4 requires regular backups, with backup data retained for the period required by national regulations and at least 5 years, stored at a separate and secure location; the accessibility of stored data must also be checked regularly, and accidental or unauthorized modification prevented by physical or electronic means.

questions.question: Under 3.6.2, when should equipment and processes be qualified or validated?

options.A: Only once, before first use, with no repetition after later repair or maintenance
options.B: Before being put into use, and after any significant change (such as repair or maintenance)
options.C: Repeated at a fixed interval every year, whether or not there has been any change
options.D: Only when a deviation occurs or the regulatory authority requires it

questions.explanation: 3.6.2 provides that equipment must be qualified and processes validated before use, and again after significant changes (for example, repair or maintenance). The scope and depth are determined by a documented risk assessment under 3.6.1, covering storage, picking and packing, and transport, among others.

questions.question: What does 4.2.4 require regarding the approval and handwriting of documents?

options.A: Documents are approved, signed, and dated by appropriate authorized persons; in principle not handwritten, with sufficient space left where handwriting is necessary
options.B: Documents are mainly handwritten so they can be adjusted in real time; approval signatures may be added afterward and dates filled in later
options.C: Only the quality manager needs to sign, and the date may be omitted to speed up version updates and quick issuance of documents
options.D: Documents may never contain handwritten content; paper forms may not be designed with any fields for filling in

questions.explanation: 4.2.4 requires documents to be approved, signed, and dated by appropriate authorized persons and in principle not to be handwritten; but where necessary, sufficient space must be provided for entries. "Never any handwritten content" is too absolute, while "mainly handwritten with signatures added afterward" and "only the quality manager signs, date omitted" violate the signature and date requirements.

questions.question: A warehouse employee finds that a batch number in a record was written incorrectly. Under 4.2.5, how should it be corrected?

options.A: Overwrite with correction fluid and rewrite, leaving a blank space for later confirmation and supervisor sign-off, with no need to note the date
options.B: Sign and date the correction, keeping the original information legible, and record the reason where appropriate
options.C: Tear out the page and refill it, destroying the old page to avoid confusion with the new one
options.D: Lightly strike it out in pencil and write in the new batch number, with a supervisor checking the correction afterward

questions.explanation: 4.2.5 requires any amendment to be signed and dated, with the original information remaining legible after the amendment, and the reason for the amendment recorded where appropriate. Overwriting, tearing out, or changing in pencil would make the original information disappear or become unreliable.

questions.question: After an SOP is revised, the old version is still posted at the workstation. Under 4.2.8, what is the correct approach?

options.A: Keep the old version at the workstation for comparison, and simply tell employees verbally that the version has changed, with no separate archiving
options.B: Immediately destroy all old versions, including archived copies, to avoid any possibility of misuse
options.C: Keep old versions only in the quality department, with no version control of procedures at all
options.D: A mechanism should prevent inadvertent use of superseded versions, and superseded procedures should be removed from workstations and archived

questions.explanation: 4.2.8 requires procedures to be subject to version control, with a system in place after revision to prevent inadvertent use of superseded versions; superseded or obsolete procedures must be removed from workstations and archived, not destroyed. Documents should also be reviewed periodically and kept up to date.

questions.question: What do 4.2.2 and 4.2.6 require for the handling and retention of personal data on natural persons such as employees and complainants?

options.A: Retained for the same period as transaction records, with no early deletion or anonymization during that period
options.B: Automatically deleted one year after a complaint is closed, with no need to assess whether retention is still needed
options.C: Deleted or anonymized once no longer needed for distribution activities, with national data protection legislation applying
options.D: Not subject to personal data protection legislation as long as they are stored in the company's internal systems, so no separate protection is needed

questions.explanation: The processing of personal data is subject to national data protection legislation, and once stored data are no longer necessary for distribution activities they should be deleted or anonymized. This differs from the retention period for ordinary documents and cannot simply be treated the same way.

questions.question: Under 4.2.9, which information must the record of each receipt or supply transaction of medicinal products include AT LEAST?

options.A: Date, name of the medicinal product, quantity, and the name and address of the supplier, customer, or consignee
options.B: Unit price, payment terms, invoice amount, and accounting codes, and the salesperson's commission and bonus
options.C: Name of the transport driver, vehicle license plate number, departure time, and the vehicle's temperature monitoring record
options.D: Customer credit limit, cumulative purchase volume over the past year, and the salesperson's visit records

questions.explanation: The minimum fields in 4.2.9 are the date, name of the medicinal product, quantity received or supplied, and the name and address of the supplier/customer/consignee, plus batch number and expiry date where required by national regulations. Records may be invoices, delivery notes, or computer form, and must be made contemporaneously; if handwritten, they must be clear, legible, and indelible.

questions.question: A new supplier offers a large quantity of a medicinal product that is normally in limited supply, at a price clearly out of line with the market. Under 5.2.4, how should the distributor respond?

options.A: A lower price helps reduce purchasing cost, so close the deal first to secure the limited supply, and carry out background checks afterward
options.B: As long as the supplier can provide business registration documents, there is no need to evaluate its sources and capability further
options.C: Treat it as a sign requiring attention, and assess the counterparty's suitability and reliability through due diligence before signing a contract
options.D: Purchase a small quantity first on a trial basis, and carry out supplier qualification and audit afterward if there are no quality problems on arrival

questions.explanation: 5.2.4 lists what due diligence should watch for when entering new contracts: the supplier's reputation and reliability, offers of medicinal products more likely to be falsified, offers of large quantities of products generally available only in limited quantities, the range of products the supplier handles, and prices outside the normal range. 5.2.3 also requires supplier qualification to be completed before purchasing, not afterward.

questions.question: Under 5.2.1, to which parties should a wholesale distributor's sources of medicinal products be limited?

options.A: Any trader or agent that can provide a batch certificate of analysis (COA) and shipping documents
options.B: The manufacturer itself only, with no products to be purchased from other wholesale distributors
options.C: Any company with medicinal product sales experience that offers a price advantage and a stable supply
options.D: Parties holding a wholesale distribution authorization, or holding a manufacturing authorization covering the product

questions.explanation: 5.2.1 provides that medicinal products may be obtained only from persons who hold a wholesale distribution authorization or a manufacturing authorization covering the product. If purchasing from other wholesalers, 5.2.2 further requires verification that they comply with GDP principles and hold an authorization. "The manufacturer itself only" is wrong because wholesalers are not a prohibited source of supply.

questions.question: A customer's orders of a narcotic medicinal product suddenly increase sharply, clearly different from past sales patterns. Under 5.3.3, how should the distributor respond?

options.A: Investigate the unusual sales pattern, and report to the regulatory authority if diversion or abuse is suspected
options.B: Ship as ordered as long as the customer holds a valid license, with no additional investigation of the reason for the order
options.C: Immediately terminate all transactions with the customer and destroy the narcotic stock already prepared
options.D: Only record it internally, because reporting is the manufacturer's responsibility and not within the distributor's scope

questions.explanation: 5.3.3 requires monitoring of transactions and investigation of any irregularities in sales patterns of products at risk of diversion (such as narcotic and psychotropic substances); where diversion or abuse may be involved, it should be investigated and, if necessary, reported to the regulatory authority. A customer holding a license does not mean unusual patterns can be ignored.

questions.question: For the same item there are two batches: batch X was received earlier but expires later, and batch Y was received later but expires earlier. Under 5.5.4, how should shipment be handled?

options.A: Ship batch X first, because it was received earlier, in line with the first-in-first-out (FIFO) principle
options.B: Ship batch Y first (FEFO); any exceptions must be documented
options.C: Ship the batch with the smaller quantity first, to clear the storage location quickly and reduce the stock-count workload
options.D: Leave it to the picker to decide, with no need to record any exception or the reason for choosing a batch

questions.explanation: 5.5.4 requires stock rotation by FEFO (first expired, first out) rather than by order of receipt (FIFO), with exceptions documented. Under 5.5.6, products close to expiry must be withdrawn from saleable stock immediately.

questions.question: Under 5.4.1 and 5.4.3, what is the purpose of receiving, and what is the precondition for moving goods into saleable stock?

options.A: Confirm that the purchase price matches the purchase order amount; once goods arrive they can be put away into saleable stock with no separate release
options.B: Test every incoming batch for assay and sterility, and put it away into the saleable stock area only after it passes
options.C: Check the quantity of goods, after which they can be moved into saleable stock immediately, with written confirmation completed and signed afterward
options.D: Confirm that the delivery is correct, comes from an approved supplier, and has no transport damage; move into saleable stock only after confirming release for sale according to a written procedure

questions.explanation: The purpose of receiving is to confirm that the delivery is correct, that the medicinal products come from approved suppliers, and that they show no visible damage from transport (5.4.1). Batches may be moved into saleable stock only after confirmation, according to a written procedure, that they are released for sale (5.4.3). A distributor's receiving does not require assay or sterility testing.

questions.question: A customer reports that a batch of medicinal product appears to have a visual defect. Under 6.2, how should the distributor handle it?

options.A: Classify it as a product quality complaint, notify the manufacturer or marketing authorization holder immediately, and assess other batches
options.B: Complete its own investigation and close the case first, and only afterward notify the manufacturer or marketing authorization holder, deciding on notification based on the result
options.C: Classify it as a distribution complaint, investigate only the transport process, and do not notify the manufacturer or holder
options.D: Log it and take no action for now, unless the customer formally requests again and submits a written request for investigation

questions.explanation: 6.2.1 requires a distinction between complaints about product quality and complaints about distribution; a quality complaint with a potential product defect must be reported to the manufacturer or marketing authorization holder immediately. 6.2.2 further requires consideration of whether other batches of the same product need to be investigated.

questions.question: 6.3.2 states that returns from pharmacies can go back to saleable stock only within an "acceptable time limit." What example does the original text give?

options.A: 3 days
options.B: 10 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 60 days

questions.explanation: 6.3.2(ii) gives 10 days as an example time limit, applying to returns from customers that do not hold a wholesale distribution authorization, or from pharmacies authorized to supply medicinal products to the public. Beyond that, the outer packaging must be unopened and undamaged, the products in date and not recalled, and there must be evidence that they were stored and transported in compliance throughout.

questions.question: A refrigerated medicinal product is returned by a customer and is to go back into saleable stock. Under 6.3.3, what is required?

options.A: An intact outer package and being in date are enough; no temperature records or other documentary evidence are needed, and the customer's own declaration suffices
options.B: A normal temperature record at the time of return is enough to return it to saleable stock, regardless of earlier transport conditions
options.C: Documentary evidence that it was kept within authorized storage conditions throughout; if there was a deviation, integrity must be demonstrated by risk assessment
options.D: Refrigerated products may never go back into saleable stock; all must be destroyed regardless of whether temperature records exist

questions.explanation: 6.3.3 requires documentary evidence that the product remained within authorized storage conditions throughout; if a deviation occurred, product integrity must be demonstrated by risk assessment. The evidence covers delivery to the customer, inspection, opening of the transport packaging, return, collection, temperature records during transport, and return to the distribution point refrigerator, among others. The temperature at the moment of return alone is not enough.

questions.question: Warehouse staff find that a batch of product is suspected to be falsified. Under 6.4, which of the following is the correct handling?

options.A: Notify the authorities and the marketing authorization holder only after an internal investigation confirms it is falsified, continuing to sell in the meantime
options.B: Return it to the original supplier and request a replacement, to avoid stock loss and keep supply stable
options.C: Put a not-for-sale label on the original shelf and wait for instructions from the authorities, with no separate segregation
options.D: Immediately halt sale and distribution, notify the authorities and the marketing authorization holder, and physically segregate and label it

questions.explanation: 6.4.1 requires immediate cessation of sale and distribution of a suspected falsified product; 6.4.2 requires immediate notification of the authorities and the marketing authorization holder (suspicion alone triggers notification, with no need to wait for confirmation); 6.4.3 requires physical segregation in a dedicated area with labelling. Once confirmed as falsified, a formal decision on removal from the market must also be made, and necessary samples retained.

questions.question: Under 6.5, which statement about evaluating the effectiveness of recall arrangements and the ability to initiate a recall is correct?

options.A: They need to be evaluated only after each actual recall has ended
options.B: Evaluating once every five years, in line with the GDP audit cycle, is sufficient
options.C: They are evaluated regularly, at least once a year, and recall operations must be able to be initiated promptly at any time
options.D: They are evaluated only when the authorities require it, with no special arrangements at other times

questions.explanation: 6.5.4 requires the effectiveness of recall arrangements to be evaluated at least annually, and 6.5.5 requires that recall operations be capable of being initiated promptly at any time. In addition, the progress of a recall must be recorded and a final report issued that includes reconciliation (6.5.9).

questions.question: Under 7.1, what is the basic requirement for the relationship between the Contract Giver and the Contract Acceptor when distribution activities are outsourced?

options.A: A verbal agreement confirmed by email is enough; a contract is signed only if a dispute arises, and details can be added later
options.B: Only the Contract Acceptor's qualification review is needed, with no written contract or separate definition of each party's responsibilities
options.C: The contract is signed and kept only by the Contract Acceptor, and the Contract Giver need not keep a copy or related documentation
options.D: There must be a written contract setting out each party's responsibilities, so that the outsourced activities are properly defined, agreed, and controlled

questions.explanation: 7.1 requires outsourced GDP activities to be correctly defined, agreed, and controlled, to avoid misunderstandings that could affect product integrity, and requires a written contract between the Contract Giver and the Contract Acceptor clearly setting out the responsibilities of each party.

questions.question: Under 7.2.2, which statement about the Contract Giver's audit of the Contract Acceptor is correct?

options.A: Audit once in the first year after signing, and thereafter rely on an annual written report from the Contract Acceptor, with no Contract Giver involvement
options.B: Audit only when a quality problem or complaint occurs, with no audits scheduled otherwise
options.C: Audit before outsourcing begins and whenever the outsourced activities change; frequency is risk-based, and audits must be permitted at any time
options.D: Audit only once beforehand, then replace further audits with a periodic written self-assessment report from the Contract Acceptor

questions.explanation: 7.2.2 requires an audit before outsourcing begins and whenever the outsourced activities change; the need for and frequency of audits are determined by risk, according to the nature of the outsourced activities, and audits must be permitted at any time. The Contract Giver must also assess the Contract Acceptor's competence and ensure through the contract that it complies with GDP.

questions.question: A contracted warehouse operator wants to subcontract part of the transport work to a third party. Under 7.3.3, how should this be handled?

options.A: Notifying the Contract Giver afterward is enough, with no prior evaluation, approval, or audit of the third party
options.B: The Contract Giver must first evaluate and approve it, and the third party must be audited (by the Contract Giver or the Contract Acceptor)
options.C: As long as the third party holds a valid business license, the Contract Acceptor may subcontract on its own
options.D: The Contract Acceptor is solely responsible, and the Contract Giver need not know about the subcontracting, take part in any evaluation, or be informed afterward

questions.explanation: 7.3.3 provides that the Contract Acceptor must not subcontract any of the work entrusted to it under the contract to a third party without the Contract Giver's prior evaluation and approval of the arrangements and an audit of the third party. The arrangements between the Contract Acceptor and the third party must also ensure that distribution information is made available in the same way as between the original Contract Giver and Contract Acceptor.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the information-provision requirements for each party under 7.2.3 and 7.3.5?

options.A: The Contract Giver provides all information needed to carry out the operations; the Contract Acceptor passes on, as per the contract, any information that may affect quality
options.B: The Contract Acceptor must provide all information on product requirements; the Contract Giver must pass any information that may affect quality to the Contract Acceptor
options.C: Each party is obliged to provide information only where the contract lists it item by item; items not listed need not be provided
options.D: Information is provided one way only, by the Contract Giver; the Contract Acceptor simply follows instructions and need not report any information back

questions.explanation: The Contract Giver must provide the Contract Acceptor with all the information necessary to carry out the operations in accordance with the specific product requirements (7.2.3); the Contract Acceptor must, as per the contract, pass to the Contract Giver any information that may affect the quality of the product (7.3.5). "The Contract Acceptor provides product requirement information and the Contract Giver passes on quality information" reverses the roles of the two parties.

questions.topic: Responsibility stays with the Contract Giver
questions.question: An outsourced warehouse operator makes an error, and the Contract Giver claims that responsibility transferred upon signing the contract. Under Chapter 7, which statement is correct?

options.A: Correct; once the contract is signed, all responsibility transfers to the Contract Acceptor, and the Contract Giver is no longer responsible for any later errors
options.B: Incorrect; the Contract Giver remains responsible for the outsourced activities, and the Contract Acceptor is responsible for the activities it undertakes
options.C: Incorrect; the Contract Acceptor bears no responsibility, because all responsibility rests with the Contract Giver
options.D: Correct, as long as the Contract Giver has completed one audit beforehand, responsibility can be transferred to the Contract Acceptor

questions.explanation: 7.2.1 states that the Contract Giver is responsible for the activities contracted out, and 7.3.1 states that the Contract Acceptor is responsible for the GDP activities it undertakes. Responsibility is not transferred by signing a contract or by auditing; each party has its own responsibilities.

questions.question: Under 8.1, what is the main purpose of carrying out self-inspection?

options.A: To monitor implementation of and compliance with GDP principles, and to propose necessary corrective measures
options.B: To evaluate individual employee performance, as the main basis for annual appraisal, rewards, and penalties
options.C: To collect compliance evidence for each authority inspection, as grounds for exemption from official inspection
options.D: To replace the qualification of suppliers and customers, reducing the cost of external audits

questions.explanation: 8.1 states that self-inspections are conducted to monitor implementation of and compliance with GDP principles and to propose necessary corrective measures. It is an internal quality monitoring tool, not a performance appraisal, and it cannot replace the qualification of suppliers and customers.

questions.topic: External audit is not a substitute
questions.question: A company engages an independent external expert to complete a comprehensive audit. Can it therefore skip self-inspection? Under 8.2.2:

options.A: Yes, external experts are more impartial and can therefore replace internal self-inspection activities
options.B: No; an audit by independent external experts may be useful, but it cannot replace self-inspection
options.C: Yes, as long as the audit report is given to management and signed off and filed
options.D: Yes, as long as the external audit covers all GDP chapters and all operational processes

questions.explanation: 8.2.2 requires self-inspection to be carried out in an impartial and detailed way by designated, competent company personnel; an audit by independent external experts may be helpful but may not be used as a substitute for self-inspection. Whether the report goes to management or covers every chapter does not change this.

questions.question: A distributor has limited staff but must complete self-inspections covering all aspects of GDP. Under 8.2.1, which statement is correct?

options.A: Cover only the areas where deficiencies have occurred in the past, and leave the rest out to save manpower
options.B: Every self-inspection must cover all aspects at once and may not be split into several, to ensure completeness, and must be finished within the same day
options.C: It may be split into several self-inspections of limited scope, but the programme must cover all aspects within a defined time frame
options.D: Cover only storage and transport as the two high-risk operations, with management review replacing the rest

questions.explanation: 8.2.1 requires a self-inspection programme covering all aspects of GDP and compliance with regulations, guidelines, and procedures within a defined time frame; self-inspections may be divided into several inspections of limited scope. Splitting is permitted, but narrowing the coverage is not.

questions.question: When a self-inspection finds a non-compliance, how should it be handled under 8.2.3?

options.A: Correct it on the spot and close it, since the problem has been removed, with no separate root cause investigation or record
options.B: The inspected department decides on its own whether to take action, and the quality unit need not follow up
options.C: Increase the frequency of the next self-inspection instead, in place of documenting and tracking CAPA
options.D: Determine the cause of the deficiency, and record corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) and follow them up continuously

questions.explanation: 8.2.3 provides that when anomalies or deficiencies are found, the cause must be determined and the CAPA documented and followed up to completion. Fixing it on the spot without examining the cause lets the deficiency recur.

questions.question: Which statement about self-inspection records and reports is consistent with 8.2.3?

options.A: All self-inspections must be recorded; the report contains all observations, and copies go to management and other relevant personnel
options.B: The report lists only the deficiencies, and copies go only to the inspected department, not to management, who need only be informed verbally
options.C: The report may contain only a summary conclusion, with detailed observations kept by the inspector and not attached
options.D: The report must be submitted to the authorities for approval before the self-inspection is considered formally complete and closed

questions.explanation: 8.2.3 requires all self-inspections to be recorded, the report to contain all observations made during the inspection, and a copy to be provided to management and other relevant persons. There is no requirement to submit it to the authorities for approval.

questions.question: Under 9.1.1, who is responsible for protecting medicinal products in transit against breakage, adulteration, and theft, and for ensuring that temperature is maintained within acceptable limits?

options.A: The receiving customer, because ownership transfers only after the goods arrive
options.B: The transport provider, bearing all of it entirely once the work is outsourced
options.C: The supplying wholesale distributor
options.D: The manufacturer, because it produced the product

questions.explanation: 9.1.1 provides that the supplying wholesale distributor is responsible for protecting medicinal products against breakage, adulteration, and theft, and for ensuring that temperature conditions in transit are within acceptable limits. Even if transport is outsourced to a third party, 9.2.9 requires the contract to cover the requirements of Chapter 7.

questions.question: A temperature deviation occurs during transport of a refrigerated medicinal product, and by arrival the temperature has returned to within range. Under 9.2.2, how should it be handled?

options.A: Because it is back in range, no report or investigation is needed, and it is simply noted in passing at the receiving check
options.B: Investigate and record only if the customer complains, and take no action if the customer does not raise it
options.C: Notify only the transport provider, who handles it and keeps the records itself, with no distributor involvement
options.D: It must be reported to the distributor and to the consignee, and the excursion investigated and handled according to an established procedure

questions.explanation: 9.2.2 requires deviations that occur during transport (such as temperature excursions or product damage) to be reported to the distributor and to the recipient of the affected medicinal products, and a procedure to be in place for investigating and handling temperature excursions. What matters is whether a deviation occurred, not the temperature on arrival.

questions.question: A driver finds no one at the consignee and leaves the medicinal products with a neighboring shop to receive on its behalf. Under 9.2.7, is this acceptable?

options.A: Yes, as long as the neighboring shop signs for them and the name of the person receiving is noted on the delivery note, with no need to notify the consignee separately
options.B: No; they must be delivered to the address stated on the delivery note and handed to the consignee, and not left at other premises
options.C: Yes, if the weather is good that day and the goods have no temperature requirement, the driver may use his own judgment
options.D: Yes, as long as the consignee is notified afterward and gives verbal consent, delivery is considered complete

questions.explanation: 9.2.7 requires delivery to the address stated on the delivery note, into the care or premises of the consignee, and medicinal products must not be left at alternative premises. Whether there is a temperature requirement, or whether notification follows afterward, does not create an exception.

questions.question: Under 9.3.2, which of the following is a factor to consider when selecting transport containers and packaging?

options.A: Expected external temperature extremes, and the estimated maximum transit time (including customs storage)
options.B: The make, age, and fuel efficiency of the transport vehicle, the cost per kilometer of transport, and maintenance records
options.C: The consignee's order value, payment terms, and past trading credit rating results
options.D: The carrier's number of employees, years in operation, and the company's market share ranking in the industry

questions.explanation: The factors in 9.3.2 include the storage and transport requirements of the medicinal products, the space required, the expected external temperature extremes, the estimated maximum transit time (including customs storage), the qualification status of the packaging, and the validation status of the transport containers. The other options have no direct bearing on product protection.

questions.question: When assembling insulated boxes for refrigerated products, which statement is correct under 9.4.6 and 9.4.7?

options.A: Cool packs should be pressed against the product to enhance cooling, and frozen and chilled packs may be mixed to save space and weight
options.B: The cool pack configuration is fixed all year round, with no seasonal adjustment and no special training or control
options.C: Cool packs can be reused as is to avoid waste; whether they have cooled sufficiently is left to the driver's judgment
options.D: Cool packs must be positioned so that the product does not come into direct contact; reuse must be controlled, and frozen and chilled packs kept separate

questions.explanation: 9.4.6 requires cool packs to be placed so that the product does not come into direct contact with them, and staff to be trained in assembling insulated boxes (including seasonal configurations) and in the reuse of cool packs. 9.4.7 requires a system to control reuse, to ensure that packs not sufficiently cooled are not used by mistake, and requires that frozen and chilled packs be physically segregated.

questions.question: Under Annex 1, a distributor gives medicinal products as a gift to a pharmacy. Which defined activity does this fall under?

options.A: Supplying: providing, selling, or donating medicinal products to wholesalers, pharmacists, or persons authorized or entitled to supply the public
options.B: Procuring: obtaining or purchasing medicinal products from manufacturers, importers, or other wholesalers and holding them in one's own warehouse
options.C: Holding: storing medicinal products, including temporary storage and custody of various medicinal products in the warehouse
options.D: Export: taking goods out of the customs territory or economic area and carrying out the related export clearance formalities

questions.explanation: Annex 1 defines Supplying as providing, selling, or donating medicinal products to wholesalers, pharmacists, or persons authorized or entitled to supply the public, so "giving as a gift to a pharmacy" falls under Supplying. Procuring is obtaining or purchasing, Holding is storing, and Export is taking goods out of the customs territory.

questions.question: Which statement best matches the Annex 1 definitions of Qualification and Validation?

options.A: Qualification proves that any procedure or process leads to the expected results; Validation concerns only whether equipment works properly and meets specifications, and must be revalidated every year
options.B: The two are entirely different, and the term Validation cannot be used to cover or include the concept and scope of qualification
options.C: Qualification proves that equipment works correctly and leads to the expected results; Validation proves that any procedure, process, equipment, material, or system leads to the expected results
options.D: Qualification refers only to confirmation of transport operations; Validation refers only to confirmation of storage operations and equipment, and the two are unrelated

questions.explanation: In Annex 1, Qualification concerns whether equipment works correctly and produces the expected results; Validation has a broader scope, covering procedures, processes, equipment, materials, activities, or systems. The Annex also notes that the term validation is sometimes extended to include the concept of qualification, so the claim that "the term Validation cannot be used to cover or include the concept and scope of qualification" is incorrect.

questions.question: Under the Temperature definitions in Annex 1, what does "Ambient" mean?

options.A: Room temperature range, i.e. +15 to +25 °C, the standard storage temperature common to all medicinal products
options.B: The actual average ambient temperature measured in the warehouse that day, recorded daily in the monitoring system
options.C: Deep-freeze conditions below -15 °C, used for vaccines and biologicals requiring frozen storage
options.D: The storage temperature required for non-refrigerated medicinal products, usually labelled store below 25 °C or 30 °C

questions.explanation: Annex 1 defines Ambient as the storage temperature required for non-refrigerated medicinal products, usually labelled on the product as store below 25 °C or 30 °C. +15 to +25 °C is the definition of Room Temperature; Cold or Cool is +8 to +15 °C, a refrigerator is +2 to +8 °C, and Deep freeze is below -15 °C.

questions.question: Under Annex 1, which statement is correct about the definition of counterfeit used outside the EU (EEA) (WHO TRS 957)?

options.A: It must contain no active ingredient at all to count as counterfeit; a product that contains ingredients does not qualify
options.B: Only branded medicinal products can be counterfeited; generics are not covered by the definition and related rules
options.C: It involves deliberate and fraudulent mislabelling with respect to identity and/or source, and may apply even if the product contains the correct ingredients
options.D: It is limited to products whose packaging or labels are forged; forgery of the contents is not covered by this definition

questions.explanation: The definition concerns medicinal products that are "deliberately and fraudulently mislabelled" with respect to identity and/or source; both branded and generic products can be counterfeited, and a product may contain the correct ingredients, the wrong ingredients, no active ingredient, insufficient active ingredient, or use fake packaging. Therefore the presence of an active ingredient alone cannot decide the matter.
questions.reference: Annex 1 Glossary: Falsified (counterfeit) medicinal product (Outside the EEA)

questions.topic: Three aspects of falsification in the EEA definition
questions.question: Of the three aspects of a falsified medicinal product in the Annex 1 EEA definition (identity, source, history), which kind of falsification does "history" refer to?

options.A: Composition and strength specifications
options.B: Records and documents relating to the distribution channels used
options.C: Manufacturer, country of manufacture, and marketing authorization holder
options.D: Packaging and labelling

questions.explanation: The three aspects in the EEA definition are identity (packaging and labelling, name, composition and strength), source (manufacturer, country of manufacture, country of origin, marketing authorization holder), and history (records and documents relating to the distribution channels used). "Composition and strength specifications" and "packaging and labelling" belong to identity, while "manufacturer, country of manufacture, and marketing authorization holder" belong to source.
questions.reference: Annex 1 Glossary: Falsified (counterfeit) medicinal product (Within the EEA)
